note: How a piece is performed (doc 24, Realizing a piece). beat: compound meters (6/8, 9/8, 12/8) count the dotted quarter as the beat, others the quarter; a piece's tempo range is in those beats per minute. rubato (per phrase, x from 0 to 1 across it): t(x) = base x (1 + push x sin(pi x)) x (1 - rit x smoothstep(0.8, 1, x)); push up to pushMax faster toward the middle, rit between ritMin and ritMax slower into the cadence (finalRit at the very end); fermata holds a marked note this many times longer, plus fermataGapS of silence after it. humanize: onset jitter up to jitterMs either way, the melody this many ms ahead on downbeats (melodyLeadMs, doc 24: about 8), velocity jitter up to velJitter either way. dynamics: the velocity of each dynamic mark, and accompanimentOffset (velocity below the melody's), counterOffset, padOffset. phraseArch: up to this much louder toward a phrase's middle. pedal: legato pedaling, lifting liftBeforeS before each chord change and pressing pressAfterS after it, released finalReleaseS after the last note ends. textures: how a generated left hand plays each chord (texture.js). weights: how often each texture is chosen (a piece may give its own weights, or a list to choose from, as variation.textures). struck: all notes together, held. arpeggio: the bass on the beat, then the upper notes one by one in eighths (quarters when the day's density ceiling is low), each held to the chord's end under the pedal; shapes up or up-down. Its notes count densityWeight each toward the day's density ceiling, so it moves in eighths by day and in slower steps (the beat, or quarters and halves in simple meters) toward evening and night. roll: a quick roll, stepMs apart, landing with the melody (before), around it (centred) or just after (after). bass-then-chord: the bass, then the chord on the next beat. broken and offbeat-dyads: the choppier figures, kept rare for this style. Each section picks a main texture; a chord keeps it with chance phraseMain, otherwise draws from the weights; a repeat section avoids the previous main with chance varyRepeat; a section's first chord is phraseStartRollBoost times likelier to roll; its last chord (the cadence) and the coda choose only from their lists. voicing: the voicing style of recipes/music/voicing.json each texture uses. Timing: notes one hand strikes together share one timing wiggle (humanize.jitterMs), so chords never smear. The ornament roll on a final chord uses roll.stepMs's upper value. pad: when a palette brings the pad in, it holds each chord's upper voices this many semitones down (octaveDown) at padOffset. layers (layers.js): the support layers of pieces that ask for them (piece.layers, piece.palette.bed and .touch). bed: a held chord on strings or the pad, per section out, in (enters from quietDb to steadyDb in the first half), swell (quietDb to peakDb across the section), steady (steadyDb) or thin (steadyDb down to quietDb, the last chord losing its top voice); dB are velocity offsets below the melody's dynamic, never below minVel; notes overlap the next chord by overlapTicks so the bed never breathes between chords, and a pitch the next chord shares is held over instead of played again; leaveLiftTicks, by bed instrument: a note the next chord does not share stops this many ticks (480 a quarter) before the change, with no overlap, so its release does not ring against the new chord (Matt, October 20, 2026); vary is the chance a section's bed moves one step quieter or louder. warm: voices close notes between low and high, under the melody, no gap wider than maxGap semitones, moving as little as possible. openFifths: the chord's bass (or root) from the lowest allowed note, stacked by these intervals (root, fifth, octave, twelfth, two octaves). touch: on a section's last chord, notes chord tones from low to high (at most an octave under the melody), at db; instruments in rolled are rolled upward rollMs apart. textures.strum (Matt, October 20, 2026: a guitar is first strummed for rhythm): when a piece names palette.strum (the guitar), it takes the chords in a guitarist's shape (src/audio/music/guitar.js) and strums them by the meter's pattern, one character per eighth of the bar: D a down stroke over every string, low to high, spread over downSpreadMs; U an up stroke over the top upStrings strings, high to low, over upSpreadMs; anything else a rest (each stroke rings until the next). Velocity steps (MIDI velocity, not dB) against the piece's dynamic: beatAccent on a down stroke on the beat, offbeatDown on one off it, up on an up stroke, downTaper less per string up a down stroke, offset under all of it. The piano then keeps only a held bass, bassOffset softer than its usual accompaniment, unless the palette says strumBass false (the guitar alone over the bed).
